overview: Cao Wei was the most powerful of the Three Kingdoms, controlling the northern heartland of China. Founded by Cao Cao's son Cao Pi, it inherited the Han administrative system and produced significant literary and military achievements.

items.text: Cao Cao and his sons Cao Pi and Cao Zhi wrote some of the finest poetry of the age, the Jian'an style named for the last Han reign period.
Cao Pi's Discourse on Literature, the first systematic essay of Chinese literary criticism, argues that writing outlasts rank and wealth.
Ma Jun builds a south-pointing chariot, a cart whose figure keeps pointing south as it turns, through gearing whose design is reconstructed with differential gears.
The tuntian system of military-agricultural colonies, begun by Cao Cao in 196 under the last Han emperor, settled soldiers and refugees on frontier land.
Administrative innovations passed to the Jin dynasty, among them the nine-rank system for grading officials, introduced in 220.
The fourteenth-century novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms later romanticized this era.

fall.text: Sima Yan forced the last Wei emperor to abdicate and founded the Jin dynasty, in the last month of 265 by the Chinese calendar, February 266 by ours.
